practice.h2: Practice with a drummer, a backing band and a looper without leaving the app.
practice.lede: 75 drum grooves in 15 genres played by real drummers, 49 backing tracks you can slow down, and a metronome that follows the same tempo as the drums.
practice.drums.p: Pick a kit and a groove, hit FILL when the chorus comes, and set the tempo from the top bar.
practice.tracks.p: 49 rock, blues and funk jams split into solo, rhythm, bass and acoustic, slowed to 0.5× without changing key or shifted ±12 semitones.
practice.metro.p: Tap tempo, time signature, subdivision and count-in, sent to the output you choose.
practice.looper.p: Up to 8 loopers per chain and 8 layers each, with undo, reverse and half or double speed.
tools.h2: A tuner and a spectrum for every input, and a mixer for every port on your interface.
tools.lede: Check pitch, frequency balance and levels while you play, without opening a second program.
tools.tuner.p: Chromatic, one per input, and it mutes the output while you tune.
tools.spectrum.p: Monitor in real time the sound coming out of each output, and pick which ones to watch.
tools.mixer.p: A fader, solo and mute for every input and output, adjustable while you play.
tools.doctor.p: Points out fizz, mud and boom against a genre reference and applies the fix with one click.
tools.di.p: Loop a dry DI file through the chain and dial the tone with your hands off the guitar.
ai.h2: Name a song and Claude builds the preset on your rig.
ai.lede: OpenRig speaks MCP, so Claude can look up the amp, cab and pedals used on the record, pick the closest gear in the catalog and save the preset while you keep playing.
ai.skillsText: Six skills in one plugin: see them on GitHub.
ai.c1.p: Researches the chain used on a song, maps it to the catalog and saves it as a new preset.
ai.c2.p: Turns your .nam and IR files, or a tone3000.com pack, into an OpenRig plugin with its manifest.
ai.c3.p: Writes the profile for your footswitch from a description or a MIDI capture.
more.h2: Two interfaces at once, hardware pedals mid-chain and an app in nine languages.
more.lede: Use what you already own: any Core Audio interface, any MIDI footswitch, any pedal on your board.
more.m1.p: Guitar into one interface, monitors out of another, both running at the same time.
more.m2.p: Send the signal out to a pedal you won't give up and bring it back mid-chain.
more.m3.p: English, Português, Español, Deutsch, Français, 日本語, 한국어, 中文 and हिन्दी.
more.m4.p: Every line is on GitHub under GPL-3.0, so anyone can read, fix or extend it.
